newsitem.title: USA: Lee Enterprises sells unit for $55 million.
newsitem.headline: Lee Enterprises sells unit for $55 million.

text.p: Lee Enterprises Inc said Friday it sold NAPP Systems Inc, its graphic arts products subsidiary, to Polyfibron Technologies Inc for $55 million.
NAPP, based in San Marcos, California, provides photopolymer printing plates and processing systems to the newspaper industry worldwide.
Lee said the sale permits it to concentrate on its core media business. It said NAPP remains an important supplier for some of its newspapers.
Lee owns and operates nine affiliated television stations and seven satellite television stations, and publishes 19 daily newspapers and 40 weekly and specialty publications.

Polyfibron is based in Billerica, Massachusetts. It was founded in 1994 to acquire the printing products business of W.R. Grace & Co. With the acquisition of NAPP, Polyfibron will have annual revenues of more than $200 million.
